title: Counit-normalized restriction on smooth section invariants and deformation endpoints
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, arbitrary finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $n\geq1$. All schemes in this statement are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are separated and finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Write $\omega_g=Rg^!A$ and $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ [def-pur-section-invariant].

Let $g:T\to B$ be smooth of pure dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with a closed section $s$. Let $a:T'\to T$ be etale over $B$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $g'=ga$, and let $s':B\to T'$ be a closed section with $as'=s$ whose square of centres over $1_B$ is Cartesian. Let $c_{g,a}:R(ga)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra^!Rg^!$ be the specified conjugate compositor [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], and use the counit-normalized etale comparison $\rho_a:Ra^!\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*$ of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. Define
$$R_a:C(g',s')\xrightarrow{Ls'^*(\rho_a c_{g,a})}Ls'^*La^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}C(g,s),$$
where the last arrow is the canonical pullback-composition constraint for $as'=s$. This is an isomorphism. For a composable second map of section pairs $b$, $R_{ab}=R_aR_b$ and $R_1=1$, with the canonical constraints; in particular this applies to open neighbourhoods of the section. These equations commute with the canonical section comparisons under base change $B'\to B$ between the stated schemes.

Let $n:N_{s'}\xrightarrow{\sim}N_s$ be the induced normal-bundle map [def-pur-normal-bundle]. The canonical map $D_{s'}T'\to D_sT$ [def-pur-dnc-section-family], on homogeneous generators $t\mapsto t$ and $f/t\mapsto a^*f/t$, is etale and preserves the augmented sections. Pullback of the same counit-normalized comparison to its section gives a family isomorphism $\widetilde R_a:F_{g',s'}\to F_{g,s}$ over $\mathbf A^1_B$, for the family objects of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. Its restrictions at $1$ and $0$ are respectively $R_a$ and $R_n$, under the canonical fibre comparisons of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry]. For the uniquely normalized deformation maps one has
$$R_n\delta_{g',s'}=\delta_{g,s}R_a.$$
The family, endpoint and composition equations are compatible with further open restriction, base restriction, and composition of etale maps of pairs. They include the rank-zero standard pair with identity comparisons. No Tate orientation or identification of $C(g,s)$ with a coefficient line is chosen.

source.place: Composition-coherence Step 1, smooth base-change coherence and normalized DNC uniqueness; chart proof Step 3, comparison of actual section and family adjunctions; returned Steps 1–5 and 8, locality part

proof.text: Transport the ordinary-etale functoriality equations through sourceComparison and the comparison pullback functor. Cancel the adjacent inverse and direct source comparisons. This proves actual pro-etale restriction identities and composition.

Use coefficientwise Rees composition to prove deformationMap composition and its mixed base-change square. Prove deformationMap identity on affine Rees charts using extendedReesAlgebraMap_id. Cancel the mono closed zero-fibre inclusion in the geometric endpoint formula to obtain normalMap identity, composition and mixed base-change naturality. Extensionality of EtaleMap then identifies induced family and normal composites; apply the restriction functoriality already proved to these pairs.
Use the section base-comparison laws for the cohomological base square and BasePasting. Adjoin the two geometric naturality equations proved in the preceding step to obtain BaseCompatibility.

Apply the four fibre squares, then use normalized specialization with precisely those hypotheses. Combine its restriction and base-change delta equations with the corresponding endpoint squares to obtain Endpoints and NormalizedBase. Take the standard rank-zero clause and assemble Composition, BaseCompatibility, Endpoints, NormalizedBase, BasePasting and RankZero.

tool_uses.why: Generic geometric Rees base-change theorem for smooth closed sections on Noetherian schemes, independent of coefficients, adjunctions, orientations or the trace-formula unit. It supplies the missing etale map-of-pairs geometry without changing the diagonal/DNC route.
Generic permanence of smooth relative dimension under composition and arbitrary base change supplies dimensions for the section and family pairs.
Generic canonical derived module pullback composition is required to identify actual section objects, rather than choosing isomorphisms.
